To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we have shown that, by combining the properties of graphene with the large tunability of large polyaromatic hydrocarbons, it is possible to engineer graphene nanostructures with remarkable charge-transfer excitons; (ii) we have shown how the properties of the charge-transfer excitations can be tuned through an appropriate choice of the functional groups; (iii) we have shown the possibility to modulate the optical properties of the charge transfer excitations through a variation of the width of the graphene

(a) the optical properties of graphene can be tuned through molecular functionalization; (b) edge-functionalization of graphene nanojunctions leads to the formation of charge-transfer excitons; (c) the optical properties are modulated through the junction width, thus spanning a large region of the UV-Vis spectrum.

(i) the optical absorption spectra of graphene nanoribbons can be tuned through functionalization; (ii) the functional groups induce charge-transfer excitons; (iii) the oscillator strength of these excitons is large, thus making these systems interesting as potential candidates for the development of optoelectronic devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the optical properties of graphene nanojunctions.
a theoretical study of the optical properties and charge-transfer excitations in edge-functionalized graphene nanojunctions.
the optical and electronic properties of graphene nanodevices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the edge-functionalized graphene junctions are a promising class of systems for the development of all-graphene opto-electronic nano-devices.
, in the context of the present work, the use of the edge-functionalized all-graphene nanojunctions is a promising strategy to design optoelectronic devices.
the edge functionalization of graphene nanoribbons allows for the engineering of a wide range of optoelectronic devices with a large variety of properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the edge-functionalized graphene nanojunctions are a very promising platform for the development of optoelectronic devices.
we show how the optical properties of graphene nanosystems can be tailored through a suitable functionalization of their edges.
the combination of graphene with molecular functional groups can lead to a new family of nanojunctions with interesting optical and electronic properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical properties of graphene can be significantly modified by functionalizing the edges of the nanosystem.
, by properly functionalizing the edges of graphene ribbons, it is possible to obtain low-energy charge-transfer excitations with large oscillator strength.

, by combining the main electronic features and the stability of graphene nanosystems with the versatility of molecular chemistry, it is possible to design a new class of optoelectronic materials with a tunable absorption profile in the UV-vis range.
